Income tax thresholds will remain frozen until 2031, adding to the growing tax burden on millions of workers and pensioners. The continued freeze on the thresholds, introduced by the Conservatives at the height of Covid and extended by Rachel Reeves in 2025, will generate billions each year through a phenomenon known as fiscal drag. Middle-earners are the most affected. Workers with salaries around £50,270 - the basic rate tax threshold - will be dragged into the higher 40 per cent rate on earnings above that mark with any future inflationary pay rises.
